([[Tinton Falls, New Jersey]]) | college = [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] (2019–2021) | draft_year = 2021 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 56 | draft_team = [[Charlotte Hornets]] | career_start = 2021 | years1 = {{nbay|2021|full=y}} | team1 = [[Charlotte Hornets]] | years2 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–2022]] | team2 = →[[Greensboro Swarm]] | years3 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team3 = [[Rip City Remix]] | years4 = [[2023–24 NBA G League season|2024]] | team4 = [[Salt Lake City Stars]] | years5 = 2024–2025 | team5 = [[Niagara River Lions]] | years6 = 2026–present | team6 = [[Johor Southern Tigers]] | highlights = * [[Canadian Elite Basketball League|CEBL]] champion ([[2024 CEBL season|2024]]) * [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team (2020) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2019 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2019]]) }} '''George Scott Lewis Jr.''' (born March 12, 2000) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[Johor Southern Tigers]] of the [[Major Basketball League Malaysia]]. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]]. ==High school career== Lewis played high school basketball for the [[Ranney School]] in [[Tinton Falls, New Jersey]]. He was unanimously ranked as a 5-star recruit from all major recruiting services for the class of 2019. On January 20, 2019, Lewis committed to the [[University of Florida]]. He is originally from [[The Bronx|The Bronx, New York]] and resides in [[Hazlet, New Jersey]].{{cite web|url=https://www.app.com/story/sports/high-school/basketball/2017/09/12/ranney-hoops-stars-scottie-lewis-and-bryan-antoine/642809001/|title=For Ranney hoops stars Scottie Lewis and Bryan Antoine, it's more than a game|website=[[Asbury Park Press]]|accessdate=March 29, 2019}} ===Recruiting=== On October 2, 2018, Lewis announced that he will be playing [[college basketball]] at the [[University of Florida]], choosing the Gators over Kentucky.{{cite web|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/2776394-5-star-sf-prospect-scottie-lewis-commits-to-florida-over-kentucky|title=5-Star SF Prospect had nine points, five rebounds and two assists as the Gators defeated [[North Florida Ospreys men's basketball|North Florida]] 74–59.{{cite news |title=Blackshear gets double-double, No. 6 Florida beats UNF 74-59 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169796 |accessdate=November 5, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 5, 2019}} On February 26, 2020, Lewis scored 18 points in an 81–66 win against [[LSU Tigers men's basketball|LSU]].{{cite news |title=Career nights for Johnson, Lewis as Florida thumps LSU 81-66 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166373 |date=February 26, 2020 |accessdate=March 23, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]]}} He had a career-high 19 points on March 7, in a 71–70 loss to [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite news |title=No. 6 Kentucky rallies from 18 down, stuns Florida 71-70 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401166388 |accessdate=March 23, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=March 7, 2020}} At the conclusion of the regular season, Lewis was named to the [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] All-Freshman Team.{{cite press release|url=https://www.secsports.com/article/28877731/sec-announces-2020-men-basketball-awards |title=SEC announces 2020 Men's Basketball Awards |publisher=Southeastern Conference |date=March 10, 2020 |accessdate=March 10, 2020}} Lewis averaged 8.5 points and 3.6 rebounds per game, leading the team in blocks (36) and finishing second to [[Keyontae Johnson]] in steals with 36.{{cite news |last1=Nettuno |first1=Tyler |title=Florida Gators Men's Basketball Profile Card: Scottie Lewis |url=https://gatorswire.usatoday.com/2020/03/15/florida-gators-mens-basketball-profile-card-scottie-lewis/ |accessdate=March 23, 2020 |work=Gators Wire |publisher=[[USA Today]] |date=March 15, 2020}} On April 6, 2020, it was announced that Lewis would return to Florida for the 2020–21 season.{{cite news |title=Scottie Lewis to return to Florida for sophomore season |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29000666/scottie-lewis-return-florida-sophomore-season |accessdate=April 6, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=April 6, 2020}} He missed three games as a sophomore after contracting COVID-19. Lewis averaged 7.9 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.6 steals per game. Following the season, he declared for the [[2021 NBA draft]] and hired an agent.{{cite news |last1=Zagoria |first1=Adam |title=Ex-Ranney School star Scottie Lewis looks to represent Shore Conference in 2021 NBA Draft |url=https://www.nj.com/setonhall/2021/06/ex-ranney-school-star-scottie-lewis-looks-to-represent-shore-conference-in-2021-nba-draft.html |access-date=August 3, 2021 |work=[[NJ.com]] |date=June 27, 2021}} ==Professional career== ===Charlotte Hornets (2021–2022)=== Lewis was selected in the second round of the [[2021 NBA draft]] with the 56th pick by the [[Charlotte Hornets]].{{cite news|first=Bob|last=Redman|title=Scottie Lewis selected in second round by the Charlotte Hornets|url=https://247sports.com/college/florida/Article/Florida-Gators-Basketball-Scottie-Lewis-selected-in-second-round-by-the-Charlotte-Hornets-168480220/|work=247 Sports|date=July 30, 2021|access-date=August 3, 2021}} On August 3, 2021, the Hornets signed him to a [[two-way contract]] for the 2021–22 season. Under the terms of the deal, he split time between the Hornets and their [[NBA G League]] affiliate, the [[Greensboro Swarm]].{{cite web|first=Quinton|last=Wash|title=Charlotte Hornets Sign Arnoldas Kulboka and Scottie Lewis To Two-Way Contracts|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/press-releases/charlotte-hornets-sign-arnoldas-kulboka-and-scottie-lewis-two-way-contracts|website=NBA.com|date=August 3, 2021|access-date=August 3, 2021}} On June 29, 2022, the Hornets declined to sign Lewis to a qualifying offer, making him an [[Free agent|unrestricted free agent]]. Lewis joined the Hornets for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]]. On July 7, 2022, he broke his left leg during a practice session. He underwent surgery to address the injury the next day and was ruled out indefinitely.{{cite web|title=Hornets' Scottie Lewis breaks leg during Summer League practice|url=https://www.nba.com/news/hornets-scottie-lewis-breaks-leg-during-summer-league-practice|website=NBA.com|date=July 8, 2022|access-date=February 22, 2023}} On October 28, 2023, Lewis was selected in the 2023 NBA G League draft by the [[Windy City Bulls]],{{cite web|title=Windy City Bulls Select Scottie Lewis in the 2023 NBA G League Draft|url=https://windycity.gleague.nba.com/news/the-windy-city-bulls-presented-by-bmo-the-nba-g-league-affiliate-of-the-chicago-bulls-selected-scottie-lewis-with-the-no-2-pick-in-the-second-round-of-the-2023-nba-g-league-draft-on-saturday-oct|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2023|access-date=December 17, 2023}} but was waived on November 8.{{cite web|title=2023-2024 Windy City Bulls Transaction History|url=https://basketball.realgm.com/dleague/teams/Windy-City-Bulls/44/Transaction_History/2024|website=RealGM.com|access-date=December 17, 2023}} ===Rip City Remix (2024)=== On January 21, 2024, Lewis joined the [[Rip City Remix]],{{cite tweet|author=Rip City Remix|title=The Rip City Remix have acquired Scottie Lewis 💿|number=1749108879450153403|user=ripcityremix|date=January 21, 2024|access-date=January 21, 2024}} but was waived nine days later.{{cite web|title=Game Notes: Rip City Remix (8-4) at Salt Lake City Stars (4-8), Jan. 30 at 6 p.m.
